ops.name: fromFixed18
ops.notice: Convert an 18-decimal fixed-point value to 127.128.

ops.name: toFixed18
ops.notice: Convert a 127.128 value to 18-decimal fixed-point.

ops.name: toFixed18Down
ops.notice: Convert a 127.128 value to 18-decimal fixed-point, rounding toward negative infinity: toFixed18 under the name that says its direction. For an amount a protocol pays out.

ops.name: toFixed18Up
ops.notice: Convert a 127.128 value to 18-decimal fixed-point, rounding toward positive infinity: ceil(x * 1e18 / 2^128). For an amount a protocol charges.

ops.name: add
ops.notice: a + b. Reverts with Overflow on signed overflow.

ops.name: sub
ops.notice: a - b. Reverts with Overflow on signed overflow.

ops.name: mul
ops.notice: floor(a * b / 2^128), the 127.128 product.
ops.reverts: Overflow() when a·b / 2^128 does not fit in int256

ops.name: div
ops.notice: a / b in 127.128, truncated toward zero.
ops.reverts: DivisionByZero() when b == 0; Overflow() when the quotient does not fit

ops.name: mulDown
ops.notice: floor(a * b / 2^128), toward negative infinity: mul under the name that says its direction.
ops.reverts: Overflow() when a·b / 2^128 does not fit

ops.name: mulUp
ops.notice: ceil(a * b / 2^128), toward positive infinity.
ops.reverts: Overflow() when the rounded product does not fit

ops.name: divDown
ops.notice: a / b in 127.128, rounded toward negative infinity. div truncates toward zero, which rounds a negative quotient up; this does not.
ops.reverts: DivisionByZero() when b == 0; Overflow() when the quotient does not fit

ops.name: divUp
ops.notice: a / b in 127.128, rounded toward positive infinity.
ops.reverts: DivisionByZero() when b == 0; Overflow() when the quotient does not fit

ops.name: exp2
ops.notice: 2^x, rounded to nearest.

ops.name: exp
ops.notice: e^x, rounded to nearest.

ops.name: exp10
ops.notice: 10^x, rounded to nearest.

ops.name: log2
ops.notice: log2(x) for x > 0, rounded to nearest.

ops.name: ln
ops.notice: ln(x) = log2(x) * ln(2) for x > 0, rounded to nearest. Reverts with OutOfRange otherwise.

ops.name: log10
ops.notice: log10(x) = log2(x) / log2(10) for x > 0, rounded to nearest. Reverts with OutOfRange otherwise.

ops.name: log2Up
ops.notice: ceil(log2(x)) for x > 0: msb(x) - 128, plus one unless x is a power of two. Exact.

ops.name: sqrt
ops.notice: sqrt(x) for x >= 0.

ops.name: pow
ops.notice: x^y = 2^(y * log2(x)) for x >= 0, rounded to nearest.
ops.reverts: OutOfRange() for x < 0; Overflow() when the result does not fit

ops.name: powu
ops.notice: x^floor(n) for an integer exponent, rounded to nearest: binary exponentiation on a 256-bit mantissa with a separate binary exponent, rounded once; when that mantissa's error bound (k + 5) 2^-255, k = |n|, straddles a rounding midpoint, the same product on a 512-bit mantissa decides. Exact whenever the true value is representable. Negative n inverts the mantissa, so x^-n is as accurate as x^n.
ops.domain: any x, any integer n = floor(n); the result must fit
ops.reverts: Overflow() when x^n does not fit; DivisionByZero() for 0^n with n < 0

ops.name: compound
ops.notice: (1 + rate)^floor(n): n periods of compounding at rate, rounded to nearest, so a per-second rate over years keeps every bit the format holds. 1 + rate is exact in 127.128 (the sum of two grid values), so nothing is lost before the exponentiation; on an 18-decimal grid the rate itself would have been the first loss.
ops.domain: rate > -1 and 1 + rate fits; any integer n = floor(n)
ops.reverts: Overflow() when 1 + rate or the result does not fit; DivisionByZero() for rate == -1 with n < 0

ops.name: cbrt
ops.notice: Cube root, defined for all x: cbrt(-x) = -cbrt(x). Rounded to nearest (decided exactly); exact for perfect cubes.

ops.name: gavg
ops.notice: Geometric mean sqrt(a * b). Reverts with OutOfRange if a * b < 0.
ops.reverts: OutOfRange() if a·b < 0; Overflow() if a·b does not fit

ops.name: hypot
ops.notice: sqrt(a^2 + b^2), checked.
ops.reverts: Overflow() if a^2 + b^2 does not fit

ops.name: inv
ops.notice: 1 / x. Reverts with DivisionByZero for x == 0.
ops.reverts: DivisionByZero() for x == 0; Overflow() when 1/x does not fit

ops.name: abs
ops.notice: |x|. Reverts with Overflow for x == -2^255, which has no positive.

ops.name: neg
ops.notice: -x. Reverts with Overflow for x == -2^255.

ops.name: min
ops.notice: Signed minimum.

ops.name: max
ops.notice: Signed maximum.

ops.name: clamp
ops.notice: min(hi, max(lo, x)). If lo > hi the result is hi, as in the Huff.

ops.name: avg
ops.notice: floor((a + b) / 2) without intermediate overflow.

ops.name: zeroFloorSub
ops.notice: max(0, a - b), with the subtraction checked.
ops.reverts: Overflow() if a - b does not fit

ops.name: dist
ops.notice: |a - b|, checked.
ops.reverts: Overflow() if a - b does not fit

ops.name: lerp
ops.notice: a + t * (b - a), checked. t is not clamped to [0, 1].
ops.reverts: Overflow() on any intermediate that does not fit

ops.name: floor
ops.notice: Largest integer <= x. Clearing the fraction bits of a two's complement word is a floor for both signs.

ops.name: ceil
ops.notice: Smallest integer >= x, as -floor(-x). Reverts with Overflow when that integer is 2^127, which does not fit.

ops.name: frac
ops.notice: x - floor(x), always in [0, 1).

ops.name: round
ops.notice: Nearest integer, halves rounded up: floor(x + 1/2). Checked.

ops.name: factorial
ops.notice: floor(n)! for 0 <= n < 34. 33! is the largest that fits.

ops.name: lambertW0
ops.notice: Principal branch of the Lambert W function, W(x) e^W(x) = x, for x >= -1/e, rounded to nearest.

ops.name: lambertWm1
ops.notice: Secondary real branch of the Lambert W function, W(x) e^W(x) = x with W(x) <= -1, for -1/e <= x < 0, rounded to nearest.

ops.name: log1p
ops.notice: ln(1 + x), rounded to nearest. The sum 1 + x is exact in 127.128, so this is ln of an exact argument, rounded once; it exists because on an 18-decimal grid the sum is where a small x loses its digits.
ops.reverts: OutOfRange() at or below -1; Overflow() if 1 + x does not fit

ops.name: expm1
ops.notice: e^x - 1, rounded to nearest, with the one subtracted before the rounding so a small x keeps its relative precision: a 27-term series at 2^-192 for |x| <= 1/16, the double-word exp beyond.

ops.name: sinh
ops.notice: sinh(x), rounded to nearest: (u + u/(1+u)) / 2 with u = e^|x| - 1 from one double-word exp at 2^-192, u/(1+u) = 1 - e^-|x| by one division, the difference taken before the one rounding. The value before rounding is within 3 units of 2^-192 plus 2^-299 relative of sinh, so the result is nearest unless sinh is within 3 2^-64 ULP (2^-44 ULP at the top of the range) of a midpoint.

ops.name: cosh
ops.notice: cosh(x), rounded to nearest: 1 + u (u/(1+u)) / 2 with u = e^|x| - 1 from one double-word exp at 2^-192 and u/(1+u) = 1 - e^-|x| by one division, which is (e^|x| + e^-|x|) / 2 summed before the one rounding. The value before rounding is within 3 units of 2^-192 plus 2^-299 relative of cosh, so the result is nearest unless cosh is within 3 2^-64 ULP (2^-44 ULP at the top of the range) of a midpoint. cosh(0) is exactly one.

ops.name: tanh
ops.notice: tanh(x), rounded to nearest. For |x| < 1/4, u / (u + 2) with u = e^(2|x|) - 1 at 2^-192; up to |x| < 46, (1 - w) / (1 + w) with w = e^(-2|x|) at 2^-192; beyond, exactly +-1, the nearest word.

ops.name: atanh
ops.notice: atanh(x) = log1p(2|x| / (1 - |x|)) / 2: the quotient at 2^-192 by one division, one unrounded logarithm of 1 + it, scaled by ln2/2 and rounded once. The value before rounding is within 2^-146 (the one-word log's 2^-145, scaled) plus 2 units of 2^-192 of atanh, so the result is nearest unless atanh is within 2^-18 ULP of a midpoint.

ops.name: erf
ops.notice: The error function. |x| <= 4 by the series, |x| > 4 as 1 - erfc(x) by the tail polynomial, both at 2^-192 and rounded once; +-1 exactly from |x| >= 9.375, where 1 - erf is below 2^-130.8 and the subtraction rounds to one.

ops.name: erfc
ops.notice: The complementary error function 1 - erf(x), computed directly for x > 4 so the tail keeps its digits down to the format's floor (erfc(9.3) is one ULP; zero from 9.375, where it is below 2^-130.8); 2 - erfc(-x) for x < 0.

ops.name: normCdf
ops.notice: The standard normal distribution function Phi(x) = erfc(-x / sqrt2) / 2, the argument scaled at 2^-192. The tail keeps its digits to the format's floor: Phi(-13) is about two ULPs, Phi(-14) rounds to zero, and Phi(x) is exactly one from x = 14. This is the N(d) of Black-Scholes; on an 18-decimal grid it is zero from about d = -8.3.
